steps.title: Draw one pixel edge

steps.question: Which value sets this edge’s length?

steps.title: Finish the pixel outline
steps.instruction: Add the remaining sides and turns.
steps.explain: Each right(90) turns a square corner. Four equal sides close the outline.
steps.question: How many times did you repeat the move and turn?

steps.title: Fill one pixel
steps.instruction: Add filling around the working loop.
steps.explain: The loop already traces the outline. begin_fill() and end_fill() color the enclosed area.
steps.question: Does end_fill() need to be inside the loop?
steps.answer: No. It runs once, after all four sides are drawn.

steps.title: Make a pixel function
steps.instruction: Move the tested commands into a function and call it.
steps.explain: x and y choose the starting corner; shade chooses the color. The square-building loop stays the same.
steps.question: Which inputs will change from one pixel to another?
steps.answer: The position inputs, and sometimes the color.

steps.title: Draw a neighbor
steps.instruction: Add a second pixel 27 units to the right.
steps.explain: Each square is 25 units wide. Moving its start by 27 units leaves a small gap.
steps.expected: Two pink squares with a gap.
steps.question: How large is the gap?

steps.title: Build a row
steps.instruction: Replace the separate calls with a loop across eleven columns.
steps.explain: col starts at 0. Multiplying col by 27 spaces each pixel 27 units from the previous one.
steps.expected: A full row of eleven squares.
steps.question: Where is column 2 placed?
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Use 1s and 0s as a pattern
steps.instruction: Draw a square only when this row’s character is 1.
steps.explain: row[col] selects one character. The if condition decides whether to draw. A 0 leaves a gap; a 1 draws a pixel.
steps.expected: Two pairs of squares: the top of the heart.
steps.question: What would changing the first 0 to 1 do?
steps.answer: It would add a square in the first column.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Add a second row
steps.instruction: Store both rows in a list. Use an outer loop to move downward.
steps.explain: The outer loop chooses a row. The inner loop reads its columns. Subtracting row × 27 moves each new row down.
steps.expected: The top two rows of the heart.
steps.question: Why subtract for y while adding for x?
steps.answer: Columns move right, where x increases. Rows move down, where y decreases.
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Build the wider middle
steps.instruction: Add three rows to the pattern data.
steps.explain: The drawing logic already works. len(pixels) adjusts the row count to match the list.
steps.expected: The top and wide middle of the heart.
steps.question: Do you need to change the loop’s repeat count?
steps.answer: No. len(pixels) counts the rows you supplied.

steps.title: Taper to the point
steps.explain: Fewer 1s in each lower row make the outline narrower. The code uses the same pixel function throughout.
steps.question: Which row creates the single bottom pixel?
steps.help: Compare the changed lines with your editor. Check parentheses, commas, and quotation marks. Indent a loop or function body four spaces.

steps.title: Add a color pattern
steps.instruction: Choose a lighter shade for every third diagonal position.
steps.explain: (row + col) % 3 is the remainder after dividing by 3. A remainder of 0 selects the lighter shade; other pixels keep the original shade.
steps.expected: A heart with a repeating two-color pattern.
steps.question: What would % 2 do to the spacing of the lighter pixels?
steps.answer: It would select positions every two diagonal counts instead of every three.
